_comment: The ops SERVICE's deploy-time role scope, held by HOST B's federation proxy.
This is the ceiling on anything that arrives from another host. The receiving proxy
checks the incoming capability claim against it -- same subset arithmetic as
chaind.subset, reimplemented in Go because the check has to happen in the proxy,
before any agent sees bytes (rung-5a spec, section 4.4). The duplication is real
and rung5a/README.md names it as a cost rather than hiding it.
Read it next to scenario/hostb-ops.yaml. The manifest says which TOOLS the service
may call; this file adds the argument constraint the manifest format cannot express,
and it is deliberately WIDER than any single goal: it is a role, fixed at deploy
time, with no idea which goal or which caller is on the other end. A caller
asserting write_config over auth_disabled is refused here even before the capability
authority is asked, because no goal this service will ever serve is allowed to touch
That the ceiling is a ROLE and not a TASK is the regression rung 5a accepts and rung
5b avoids. A hostile-but-enrolled host cannot exceed this list -- and can do
anything inside it, for any goal it cares to name.
